data.best_text: April to June and September to October. July and August are hot and full of tourists.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: Alfama, the castle and an afternoon in Belém.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time for Belém at an easy pace, the viewpoints and an evening in Bairro Alto.

stay.label: Five days
stay.text: Add Sintra and a day on the coast in Cascais.

areas.name: Baixa and Chiado
areas.text: Flat and central, with the metro in every direction. The most expensive.

areas.name: Alfama
areas.text: The old quarter below the castle. Beautiful but steep and full of stairs.

areas.name: Bairro Alto
areas.text: A bar district that is noisy until late. Good for going out, worse for sleeping.

areas.name: Príncipe Real
areas.text: Quieter streets with cafés and shops, walking distance to Chiado.

transport.mode: The metro's red line from the airport
transport.text: The airport is 7 km from the centre. A ride costs 1.90 euros plus 0.50 euros for the Navegante card. For Baixa and Rossio you change lines, allow 20–35 minutes.
Lines 744 and 783 take 30–45 minutes depending on traffic.
Top up a Navegante card at a machine. The metro runs roughly 6.30 am–1 am and a 24-hour ticket costs 7.25 euros.

month_notes: Mild but rainy. Few tourists and low prices.
Spring begins. Good weather for walking the hills.
Warm without the heat. Best for the viewpoints.
Warm and dry, before the high-summer crowds.
Warm with long evenings. More tourists.
The hottest, and many Lisbon residents are away.
The heat eases and the sea is warm.
Mild and clear, with fewer tourists.

prices.summary: Cheaper than at home, especially beer, coffee and local transport. Accommodation has become expensive.
tips: A pastel de nata costs around 1.30 euros and a bifana around 2.50 according to a couple who lived in the city.
The church at Jerónimos Monastery is free. It is the cloister that costs money.

rows.note: Single metro ticket with a Navegante card. Numbeo gives 2.10 euros.

PT-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
PT-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not count as a travel document.
PT-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen. A Swedish driving licence is not normally accepted as a travel document.

PT-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
PT-fakta-mobil.summary: EU roaming: the same price as in Sweden.
PT-fakta-mobil.body: You pay as at home for calls, texts and data, but the operator may set a cap on data abroad.

PT-lissabon-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport to the centre by metro
PT-lissabon-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: The red line runs from the airport. 1.90 euros plus 0.50 for the card.
PT-lissabon-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: Aeroporto station is the end of the line. For Baixa, Chiado and Alfama you change to the green line at Alameda or the blue line at São Sebastião. The metro runs roughly 6.30 am–1 am.

PT-lissabon-fakta-navegante.title: Buy a Navegante card straight away
PT-lissabon-fakta-navegante.summary: The card costs 0.50 euros and is topped up at the machines in the metro.
PT-lissabon-fakta-navegante.body: It is valid on the metro, buses and trams. You can also tap a contactless bank card in the metro for 1.92 euros per ride.

PT-lissabon-jeronimos.name: Jerónimos Monastery
PT-lissabon-jeronimos.summary: A World Heritage Site in Belém. The cloister costs 18 euros, the church is free.
PT-lissabon-jeronimos.body: One of the finest examples of Manueline architecture. The ticket is for a set time, so book the first slot of the morning.

PT-lissabon-belemtornet.name: Belém Tower
PT-lissabon-belemtornet.summary: A 16th-century fortification by the river Tagus. 8 euros for adults.
PT-lissabon-belemtornet.body: Children under 12 enter free. There is no lift and no toilets in the tower.

PT-lissabon-sao-jorge.name: Castelo de São Jorge
PT-lissabon-sao-jorge.summary: The castle on the hill above Alfama, with a view over the whole city.
PT-lissabon-sao-jorge.body: Open 9 am–9 pm according to the ticket site.

PT-lissabon-sparvagn-28.name: Tram 28
PT-lissabon-sparvagn-28.summary: The yellow tram through the old quarters.
PT-lissabon-sparvagn-28.body: Included in the Lisboa Card together with the metro, buses and the Santa Justa lift.

bakverk-pastel-de-nata.name: Pastel de nata
bakverk-pastel-de-nata.hint: A small custard tart in puff pastry, best warm with cinnamon.

mat-bifana.name: Bifana
mat-bifana.hint: Pork in a bread roll, eaten standing at the counter.

mat-bacalhau.name: Bacalhau
mat-bacalhau.hint: Dried and salted cod, in hundreds of variations.

fardmedel-gul-sparvagn.name: Yellow tram
fardmedel-gul-sparvagn.hint: The old cars that climb Lisbon's hills.

PT-lissabon-ide-belem.title: A morning in Belém
PT-lissabon-ide-belem.body: Book the first slot at Jerónimos Monastery and then walk along the river to Belém Tower.

PT-lissabon-ide-borgen.title: Sunset from the castle
PT-lissabon-ide-borgen.body: Walk up through Alfama to Castelo de São Jorge late in the afternoon.

PT-lissabon-ide-nata.title: Pastel de nata test
PT-lissabon-ide-nata.body: Buy one each at three different bakeries and vote for the best.

PT-lissabon-ide-sparvagn.title: Ride tram 28
PT-lissabon-ide-sparvagn.body: Board early in the morning before the queues, and keep an eye on your bag.

PT-present-sardiner.name: Tinned sardines
PT-present-sardiner.body: The tins have colourful labels and survive a suitcase.

PT-present-kakel.name: Azulejo
PT-present-kakel.body: A hand-painted tile. Buy newly made ones, not old tiles from house façades.

PT-present-kork.name: Something in cork
PT-present-kork.body: Wallets, coasters and bags in Portuguese cork.
